# Custom Goods Logistics

Custom Goods Logistics (.) is a Warehousing and Storage company. Custom Goods Logistics is a company that provides comprehensive logistics solutions, including warehousing, transportation, freight forwarding, and advanced supply chain technology. Custom Goods Logistics employs 368 people, founded in 1962. Headquartered in Carson, California, United States. Its workforce is distributed across United States and India.

## About

Custom Goods Logistics is a full-service logistics company with a refined focus on Warehousing, Transportation, and Custom Examination Sites, with over 34 warehouses nationally. We are uniquely positioned to offer comprehensive logistics solutions with a personal touch.

We serve our customers one shipment at a time by challenging ourselves to be the benchmark service provider of customized supply chain solutions with our strategic anchors: Data-Driven, Personal Touch, and Timely Customer Solutions.

Our core values underpin us as individuals, and as a company, we place people at the center of all we do. We have established over 60 years of rich experience and deep relationships following these values. As a number one strategic partner, our customers benefit from our unrivaled dedication to customer excellence.

- [2026-10-06 · Posted · 3 reactions] [Once your container clears the vessel, a clock starts. You have a...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/custom-goods_drayage-transload-demurrage-activity-7513252047283023872-5Xv4)
  > Once your container clears the vessel, a clock starts. You have a few free days to pick it up, unload it, and get the empty back to the line. Miss that window and the per-diem charges begin, and they don't stop until the box is back.
  >
  > Here's the trap: at busy gateways like Los Angeles and Long Beach, the expensive delays usually aren't at the vessel. They're on the land side:
  > >Appointment slots that fill up on peak discharge days.
  > >Chassis that aren't where you need them.
  > >Empty return restrictions that limit when and where the line will take the box back.
  >
  > Any one of those can push a container past its last free day even when the port looks fluid.
  >
  > Why it matters: you can't fix a land-side problem with an ocean-side plan. The fastest way to protect your free time is to unload close to the port and return the empty quickly, instead of trucking a loaded ocean container hundreds of miles inland and back.
  >
  > That's the whole idea behind transload. Strip the box near the terminal, move your freight inland in domestic trailers, and give the carrier's equipment back fast.

- [2026-09-24 · Posted · 10 reactions] [Demurrage and detention are not the same charge. Both are penalties...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/custom-goods_demurrage-detention-drayage-activity-7508904278091161600-DQTd)
  > Demurrage and detention are not the same charge. Both are penalties for going past your free time, but they're two different clocks:
  >
  > Demurrage is the charge for a container sitting inside the terminal past free time. It's the terminal's meter, running while the box waits to be picked up.
  >
  > Detention is the charge for holding the carrier's equipment outside the terminal too long before you return the empty. That's the carrier's per-diem.
  >
  > One is "you didn't pick it up fast enough." The other is "you didn't give it back fast enough."
  >
  > Free time is short, often 3 to 7 days, and some Long Beach terminals no longer exempt weekends, so you have less runway than the tariff suggests. Rates commonly run $150 to $300 per container per day and climb on tiered schedules. A 5-day overrun at $200 a day is $1,000 a box, before chassis per-diem.
  >
  > Why it matters: the two charges call for different fixes. Demurrage is about speed of pickup and appointment availability. Detention is about how fast you strip the box and return the empty.
  >
  > This is exactly what we're built to solve. We run 50,000+ drayage moves a year out of Los Angeles and Long Beach on our own equipment, and transload near the port so your freight moves inland while the empty goes back fast. Both clocks, stopped by one partner.
  > #Demurrage #Detention #Drayage #Transload #SupplyChain #Logistics #CustomGoodsLogistics

- [2026-09-22 · Posted · 2 reactions] [A retailer chargeback isn't a fee. It's a leak in your profit...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/custom-goods_retailcompliance-chargebacks-retail-activity-7508180123548807168-59TK)
  > A retailer chargeback isn't a fee. It's a leak in your profit margins.
  >
  > If you sell into major retailers, you've signed a vendor compliance guide. Break its rules and the retailer deducts a penalty straight off your invoice. The most common triggers:
  > >Late or early delivery outside the appointment window.
  > >ASN errors, or missing and incorrect advance ship notices.
  > >Label and barcode problems, including wrong or unscannable GS1 labels.
  > >Carton and packaging violations, like overweight cartons or the wrong pallet configuration.
  > >Routing guide violations, like using the wrong carrier or mode.
  >
  > Individually they look small. Across thousands of POs a year they add up to real money, and they quietly damage your scorecard with the retailer, which is the bigger cost.
  >
  > Why it matters: most chargebacks are preventable. They come from execution gaps, not bad luck. Accurate ASNs, compliant labeling, and hitting the delivery window handle the majority of them.
  >
  > This is where a disciplined 3PL earns its keep, and it's how we run. Accurate ASNs, retailer-compliant labeling and packaging, and on-time-in-full execution against the routing guide, all tracked in our WMS. For one footwear brand, tightening this cut compliance errors by 84%.
  >
  > If chargebacks are eating your margin, they're worth auditing line by line, and we can help you do it.
  > #RetailCompliance #Chargebacks #Retail #CPG #SupplyChain #Logistics #CustomGoodsLogistics

# Quik Pick Express "A Custom Goods Logistics Company"

Quik Pick Express "A Custom Goods Logistics Company" is a Transportation, Logistics, Supply Chain and Storage company. Quik Pick Express "A Custom Goods Logistics Company" employs 51 people (-5.6% YoY, -3 people) and has an annual revenue of $16.2M, founded in 1988. Headquartered in Carson, California, United States, with an office in Oakland.

## About

Quik Pick Express, LLC, a division of Custom Goods Logistics (custom-goods.com), is a leading provider of third-party logistics (3PL) solutions, specializing in warehousing and trucking services across California. Since its founding in 1988, Quik Pick Express has expanded from a single facility in Carson, CA, to eight strategically located warehouses across the Los Angeles/Long Beach and Oakland corridors, offering over 750,000 sq. ft. of space.

We are committed to sustainability with our fleet of Green Trucks, supporting the AQMD Clean Truck initiative, which aligns with our ongoing mission to reduce our environmental impact.

Serving a global network of customers, including shippers, beneficial cargo owners, ocean carriers, intermodal companies, customs house brokers, and freight forwarders, Quik Pick Express is equipped to meet all your transportation, warehousing, and logistics needs. We seamlessly connect marine terminals, rail hubs, and distribution centers throughout California to ensure efficient, reliable service.

Our comprehensive service offerings include:

--Harbor drayage with company-owned tri-axle and four-axle tractors
--Local trucking (53ft dry van, flatbeds, LTL/FTL)
--Import/export consolidations
--Hazmat transport
--Heavy lift & over-dimensional drayage & transloading
--CFS, bonded carrier, and full transloading capabilities
--With a strong focus on flexibility, reliability, and sustainability, Quik Pick Express continues to deliver tailored logistics solutions to meet the evolving needs of the global supply chain.

properties.name: Quik Pick Express "A Custom Goods Logistics Company"
properties.description:
Quik Pick Express, LLC, a division of Custom Goods Logistics (custom-goods.com), is a leading provider of third-party logistics (3PL) solutions, specializing in warehousing and trucking services across California. Since its founding in 1988, Quik Pick Express has expanded from a single facility in Carson, CA, to eight strategically located warehouses across the Los Angeles/Long Beach and Oakland corridors, offering over 750,000 sq. ft. of space.

We are committed to sustainability with our fleet of Green Trucks, supporting the AQMD Clean Truck initiative, which aligns with our ongoing mission to reduce our environmental impact.

Serving a global network of customers, including shippers, beneficial cargo owners, ocean carriers, intermodal companies, customs house brokers, and freight forwarders, Quik Pick Express is equipped to meet all your transportation, warehousing, and logistics needs. We seamlessly connect marine terminals, rail hubs, and distribution centers throughout California to ensure efficient, reliable service.

Our comprehensive service offerings include:

--Harbor drayage with company-owned tri-axle and four-axle tractors
--Local trucking (53ft dry van, flatbeds, LTL/FTL)
--Import/export consolidations
--Hazmat transport
--Heavy lift & over-dimensional drayage & transloading
--CFS, bonded carrier, and full transloading capabilities
--With a strong focus on flexibility, reliability, and sustainability, Quik Pick Express continues to deliver tailored logistics solutions to meet the evolving needs of the global supply chain.
